Prohibited information flow: Transactions occurring after the scoring time influence a model evaluated on earlier or contemporaneous observations.
Likely distortion: Inflated discrimination and understated temporal degradation because training and test are treated as exchangeable.
Control implemented in this study: Chronological outer folds with expanding historical training and untouched future test; random splits only as an explicitly labelled comparator.
Minimum audit evidence: Minimum/maximum timestamps for every block; proof max development time < min test time; row counts and prevalence by fold.

Prohibited information flow: Fraud labels, chargebacks, investigation outcomes, or target-derived statistics are used before operational maturation.
Likely distortion: Unrealistically clean supervision, especially for recent transactions, and exaggerated value of fraud-history features.
Control implemented in this study: Label-cutoff rules and 0-, 7-, 14-, and 30-day confirmation-delay scenarios; post-resolution variables excluded.
Minimum audit evidence: For each target-derived feature: event time, label-confirmation time, imposed delay, latest admissible label timestamp.

Prohibited information flow: Aggregates or joins include the current event, later events, or values generated after the prediction timestamp.
Likely distortion: Look-ahead bias in velocity, frequency, entity-risk, graph, and behavioural features.
Control implemented in this study: Global chronological ordering followed by strictly lagged cumulative/rolling features; current-row exclusion; point-in-time entity histories.
Minimum audit evidence: Feature-level cutoff; join condition; tests showing future-row perturbations cannot change an earlier feature vector.

Prohibited information flow: The same event, near duplicate, customer, card, merchant pattern, or derived record crosses development/evaluation contrary to the estimand.
Likely distortion: Memorisation mistaken for generalisation; uncertainty understated.
Control implemented in this study: Transaction-ID uniqueness checks, identity joins, duplicate screening, chronological entity histories; entity-blocked evaluation when required by estimand.
Minimum audit evidence: Cross-block overlap counts for IDs/hashes; duplicate report; explicit statement whether previously observed entities are permitted.

Prohibited information flow: Imputation, scaling, encoding, dimensionality reduction, feature selection, vocabulary construction, or missingness rules use later observations.
Likely distortion: Evaluation data shape the representation before fitting, producing optimistic/irreproducible performance.
Control implemented in this study: Every fitted transformation learned from training and applied unchanged later; unknown categories handled prespecifically.
Minimum audit evidence: Fitted-object provenance, training row hashes, learned dictionaries and imputation/scaling parameters, fit/transform code.

Prohibited information flow: Over/undersampling, synthetic generation, case-control selection, or class balancing occurs before splitting or alters evaluation prevalence.
Likely distortion: Cases can cross partitions; precision, calibration, and operational utility cease to represent natural deployment prevalence.
Control implemented in this study: Sampling confined to historical training; validation, calibration, and test remain unsampled at natural prevalence.
Minimum audit evidence: Pre/post-sampling counts by block; seeds; proof no sampled/synthetic record enters evaluation.

Prohibited information flow: Hyperparameters, features, model classes, or stopping iterations are chosen using the final test.
Likely distortion: Selection bias: reported test score becomes the maximum of repeated noisy comparisons.
Control implemented in this study: Validation separated from final test; configurations fixed before scoring; calibration analysis separates fit from selection.
Minimum audit evidence: Search space, objective, seeds, validation indices, candidate count, immutable final-test access log.

Prohibited information flow: Test labels fit or choose calibrators, probability cutoffs, alert budgets, or cost policies.
Likely distortion: Artificially improved Brier/log-loss and operational metrics.
Control implemented in this study: Calibrators fitted on later development windows and selected without test access; budgets prespecified; test labels only for final evaluation.
Minimum audit evidence: Calibration timestamps; selection criterion; prespecified budget/cost rule; parameter file; test-access record.

Prohibited information flow: Holdout results guide revisions, reruns, metric/subgroup choice, or selective reporting.
Likely distortion: Adaptive overfitting to the benchmark and hidden multiplicity.
Control implemented in this study: Frozen analysis plan, complete fold reporting, fixed metrics, manifests/checksums, separation of diagnostic from confirmatory outputs.
Minimum audit evidence: Versioned protocol/code; complete run ledger; all prespecified outcomes/folds; qualification for multiplicity.
